html:
The traffic light is the other exercise every simulator has, and the reason is not the lamps: six outputs in a fixed order is a morning’s work. The reason is everything around them. A pedestrian button that must be remembered until the right moment and then forgotten. Loops in the road that turn a fixed cycle into one that answers to traffic. An amber that is never shortened, an all-red that has to be long enough for the last car to clear, a WALK that has to end early enough for the slowest walker, and a box in the cabinet that will take the whole intersection away from your program the instant it shows two greens. Logix Connect has the street for it, under File → New Project → Classic: traffic intersection: a real crossing on grass, with cars and pedestrians who do what cars and pedestrians do. The scene comes with its tags made and an empty routine. The program below is the reference (File → Load Reference Solution: Traffic intersection), built in the order the classic exercise asks: the timed cycle, then the walk signs, then the loops, then flash.

The street

The Intersection part is under Classic scenes. Its properties are the traffic: cars per minute on each approach (16 in the scene), whether pedestrians arrive by themselves and how often, whether the cabinet has a conflict monitor, Long roads (on in a new scene), and the day: Day length and Start hour. Its I/O is what a signal cabinet wires, and the N/S heads share outputs the way the two heads for one road share a load switch:

SignalMeaning
NS_Car inputA car on either N/S approach loop (northbound or southbound)
EW_Car inputA car on either E/W approach loop
NS_Ped_PB inputPedestrian button to cross the E/W road (walk along N/S), 1 while pressed
SignalMeaning
EW_Ped_PB inputPedestrian button to cross the N/S road (walk along E/W), 1 while pressed
MMU_Fault inputConflict monitor tripped: the cabinet is in red flash until the MMU is reset (click the cabinet)
NS_Red outputN/S heads: red
NS_Yellow outputN/S heads: amber
NS_Green outputN/S heads: green
EW_Red outputE/W heads: red
EW_Yellow outputE/W heads: amber
EW_Green outputE/W heads: green
NS_Walk outputWALK for the crossings along N/S (over the E/W road)
NS_DontWalk outputDON’T WALK for those crossings
EW_Walk outputWALK for the crossings along E/W (over the N/S road)
EW_DontWalk outputDON’T WALK for those crossings

NS means along N/S. NS_Green is the green for cars travelling north and south; NS_Walk is the WALK for pedestrians travelling north and south, who cross the E/W road, and so needs the E/W road red. That is how the original exercise names them and it is the only naming that lets the conflict rule be stated in one line: a WALK may never be shown with the green of the road it crosses.

The cars are the part’s physics, not programmable. They arrive at random, queue behind each other, stand on the loops, go on green and stop on red. On amber they make one decision when it appears, as a driver does: a car close to the line at speed goes through, the rest stop, and the decision is kept. A car that is through the stop line is committed and crosses whatever the lamps do. Two cars in the box from both roads at once is a collision: logged, counted, and only the program can cause it. The pedestrians press once (0.4 s), again after twenty seconds, and give up after a minute; a WALK for their crossing starts them, and kerb to kerb takes six seconds whatever the sign does meanwhile. A car through the crosswalk while they are on it is counted the same way as a collision.

The conflict monitor is the part of a real cabinet most people have never heard of. It is a separate box, the MMU, that watches the load switches, not the controller, and if it ever sees green or amber on both roads, or a WALK against the green that crosses it, for a third of a second, it drops the whole intersection into red flash in hardware and holds it there, whatever the controller says, until a technician resets it at the cabinet. The part does exactly that: MMU_Fault goes to 1, the heads flash red regardless of your outputs, and a click on the cabinet resets it. Turn it off in the properties if you want to see what your mistake would have done.

Three views, day and night

Like every scene, the crossing has three views. The side view stands on the south side of Main St and looks north up 1st Ave: a low oblique elevation in which x is the plan’s x and a thing further north stands a little higher, so the cross street runs across the picture, the avenue’s cars stand one behind the other up it, the northbound heads face you with their three lamps and the others are seen from the side or behind. The near side of Main St is cut away so nothing hides the crossing. The cabinet and the walk buttons work in it as they do in the plan.

The day runs on the run’s clock, as the parking gate’s does: 24 minutes of run time make a whole day by default, twelve of daylight and twelve of night, with a dusk and a dawn between. At night the lamps carry the picture: every lit signal lamp throws its colour on the road, the walk signs glow, the street lights pool on the pavement, the filling station’s canopy and the shopfronts light, and every car runs with its headlights (their beams cut short by the car in front) and its tail lights, bright brake lights while it waits at the line. In 3D the sky goes to night blue, the office and shop windows light and the lamps come on. None of it changes what the program sees.

Try it: rush hour at dusk

Set Cars per minute to 30 and Start hour to 17, and run your program. Watch the queues on the long approaches: a fixed cycle that was fine at 8 cars a minute leaves cars waiting through two greens now, and the loops are what fix it. Then switch to the side view and watch the northbound queue stand up the avenue.

The program’s index

As with the elevator, the main routine is a table of contents. Two routines run every scan regardless (demand, and the monitor), the heads and the signs follow the step, and the cycle itself is held while the intersection flashes:

Exercise 1: the timed cycle

Six steps in a DINT, a timer for each, and a transition rung that moves the step on when its timer is done. The timers are conditioned on their step, so each resets when its step leaves and starts clean when it comes back; that is the whole trick of a step sequencer with TONs. Read the Cycle routine first with the loop and request contacts covered by your thumb: what remains is a fixed-time signal, which is the first exercise.

Exercise 2: the walk signs

A pedestrian request is a latch: pressed for 0.4 s, wanted for up to a minute. It is served only in the right step, only for a walk interval, and only if it existed when the step began; after the interval the sign flashes DON’T WALK for the rest of the green, the clearance for whoever is still crossing, and the request is cleared when the step ends.

Exercise 3: vehicle actuation

The loops turn the fixed cycle into a responsive one, and the change is small: two contacts in two transition rungs. The main road rests in green: its green ends after the minimum only when the side road has demand (a car on a loop or a pedestrian request), or at the maximum. The side road’s green ends after its minimum when the main road is waiting, or when its own loops have been clear (gap-out: nobody left to serve), or at its maximum. With nobody about, the main road stays green all night.

The heads

Exercise 4: flash

Flash is two things here. The selector on the cabinet puts the intersection into flashing red on purpose (night mode, or a technician working); the MMU puts it there by force. In both the program holds the cycle at all-red, so when flash ends the drivers get a clearance interval and then a green, never a green out of nowhere.

Guided: the intersection

The crossing opens with its guided track on as well (File → New Project → Classic: traffic intersection, or Guided → Guide This Scene: the Intersection). Seven lessons: Init (all-red on power-up), Heads (the reds from the step: both red, nothing else), Cycle (E/W gets its green and the cycle goes round), Demand (a car parked on a loop and a button press make requests), Walk (WALK comes with the matching green, DON’T WALK otherwise), Monitor (the run lamp, and the selector puts the heads in flash) and Ready. Heads comes before Cycle, which is backwards from the exercise order above and deliberate: with the lamps written first, the first thing the Cycle lesson shows you is a green, and from then on every rung is checked against a crossing you can watch. The Cycle’s JSR goes into the index as XIO(Flash)JSR(Cycle), so the flash lesson at the end has something to hold.

Try it: hints only

Do the Cycle lesson without pressing Show rung once. The comments give the step numbers and the times; Hint gives the timers and the compares; the shape of a transition rung, EQU(?,?)XIC(?) [XIC(?),XIC(?)]MOV(?,?), is the same rung four times with different numbers. The tally at the routine’s heading should read 14 written (14 without the text), and if it does, you have written a step sequencer, which is most of industrial programming.

Run it

Run mode: both roads red for two seconds, then E/W green. Cars arrive, queue, and the main road settles into green; the first side-road car trips its loop, N/S goes amber, all-red, and the side road gets its green. A pedestrian presses at a corner; the WALK comes with the next matching green, they cross, the sign flashes DON’T WALK behind them. Let it run ten minutes and read the count at the top of the part: through, walked, and no conflicts.

Try It

Add a left-turn phase: a protected N/S left on a fourth lamp (a green arrow) before the N/S through green, with its own minimum and its own all-red, and work out what the MMU would need to know about it. Then the exercise as the original sets it: throw away the Cycle routine and build the six steps with a single SQO sequencer and one timer. The car wash chapter, when it comes, is that instruction’s home.

Machine faults on the intersection

Tools → Inject Machine Fault… lists the faults that belong to the parts on this floor. Each has a fault card: the symptom, what to watch in the I/O to confirm it, the repair, and what a program should do about it. Repair on an active fault removes its cause the way a technician would; whether the machine runs again is up to the program. The failed red load switch is the one the cabinet catches for you: the conflict monitor sees the dark approach (RED FAIL) and flashes the intersection, and the reference’s Monitor routine follows it into flash. The detectors and the button are yours to catch.

FaultWatchRepairThe program should
Intersection: N/S red load switch failed
The program commands N/S red but no
voltage reaches the heads: the N/S
approach goes dark. The conflict monitor
detects it (RED FAIL) and puts the cabinet
into flash.NS_Red 1 from the program, the N/S heads dark, then MMU_Fault 1.Replace the load switch (Repair), then reset the conflict monitor at the cabinet.MMU_Fault: flash mode, the cycle held at all-red, the fault lamp. The Monitor routine of the reference does exactly this.
Intersection: E/W loop detector stuck
on
The E/W detector reports a car whether
there is one or not.EW_Car 1 with the E/W loops empty; the main road’s green is cut short every cycle.Retune the detector (Repair).A detector on for longer than any car sits (two minutes) is treated as failed: alarm, and run that road on its maximum (max recall).
Intersection: E/W loop detector dead
The E/W detector never reports a car.Cars queued on E/W, EW_Car 0: they wait for the main road’s maximum.Replace the detector (Repair).A detector that never changes for a long time is treated as failed: give its road a fixed recall so nobody waits for ever.
FaultWatchRepairThe program should
Intersection: N/S push button stuck in
The N/S pedestrian button is jammed in.NS_Ped_PB 1 all the time: a WALK every N/S green.Free the button (Repair).A button held for more than ten seconds is ignored and alarmed.

rungs.head: Rung 0
rungs.comment: THE INDEX. Init once on the first scan; then every scan: what is waiting (Demand), the cycle while not flashing, the heads, the walk signs, the monitor
rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung runs the routine Init.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. JSR(Init) Jump to Subroutine does: runs the routine Init. The routine is scanned at this point, then the scan comes back here.

pats.t: Part of the index: one call, one job.
pats.why: The main routine calls each routine in turn. A routine that is not called is not scanned, however correct its rungs are.
pats.think: a running order on a clipboard: the main routine reads it top to bottom, and each line sends you to a page that does one job.
pats.watch: A new routine does nothing until a JSR calls it. If a routine’s rungs never highlight online, look here first.

rungs.head: Rung 1
rungs.comment: Loops and buttons into requests
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung runs the routine Demand.
rungs.ltr: 1. JSR(Demand) Jump to Subroutine does: runs the routine Demand. The routine is scanned at this point, then the scan comes back here.

pats.t: Part of the index: one call, one job.
pats.why: The main routine calls each routine in turn. A routine that is not called is not scanned, however correct its rungs are.

rungs.head: Rung 2
rungs.comment: The step sequence, held while the intersection flashes
rungs.words: When Flash (Flash mode: the selector, or the conflict monitor has tripped) is off, the rung runs the routine Cycle.
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Flash) Examine If Open asks: true when Flash is off.
  2. JSR(Cycle) Jump to Subroutine does: runs the routine Cycle. The routine is scanned at this point, then the scan comes back here.

pats.t: Part of the index: one call, one job.
pats.why: The main routine calls each routine in turn. A routine that is not called is not scanned, however correct its rungs are.

rungs.head: Rung 3
rungs.comment: Red, amber, green from the step
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung runs the routine Heads.
rungs.ltr: 1. JSR(Heads) Jump to Subroutine does: runs the routine Heads. The routine is scanned at this point, then the scan comes back here.

pats.t: Part of the index: one call, one job.
pats.why: The main routine calls each routine in turn. A routine that is not called is not scanned, however correct its rungs are.

rungs.head: Rung 4
rungs.comment: WALK / DON'T WALK from the step and the requests
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung runs the routine Walk.
rungs.ltr: 1. JSR(Walk) Jump to Subroutine does: runs the routine Walk. The routine is scanned at this point, then the scan comes back here.

pats.t: Part of the index: one call, one job.
pats.why: The main routine calls each routine in turn. A routine that is not called is not scanned, however correct its rungs are.

rungs.head: Rung 5
rungs.comment: Flash mode, the flasher, the cabinet lamps, Reset
rungs.words: Every scan, the rung runs the routine Monitor.
rungs.ltr: 1. JSR(Monitor) Jump to Subroutine does: runs the routine Monitor. The routine is scanned at this point, then the scan comes back here.

pats.t: Part of the index: one call, one job.
pats.why: The main routine calls each routine in turn. A routine that is not called is not scanned, however correct its rungs are.

rungs.head: Init · Rung 0
rungs.comment: FIRST SCAN: start in all-red (step 2). Nobody is ever shown a green on power-up; the cycle goes to E/W from here, and the requests are cleared

pred.q: S:FS is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written, NS_Ped_Req is unlatched, EW_Ped_Req is unlatched, T_NSG is reset, T_NSX is reset, T_EWG is reset, T_EWX is reset, T_NSW is reset and T_EWW is reset.

rungs.words: When S:FS is on, the rung puts 2 into Step (The cycle: 0 N/S green, 1 N/S amber, 2 all red, 3 E/W green, 4 E/W amber, 5 all red), unlatches NS_Ped_Req (A pedestrian wants to cross along N/S (latched by the button, cleared when served)), unlatches EW_Ped_Req (A pedestrian wants to cross along E/W), resets T_NSG (N/S minimum green (8 s)), resets T_NSX (N/S maximum green (20 s)), resets T_EWG (E/W minimum green (7 s)), resets T_EWX (E/W maximum green (15 s)), resets T_NSW (N/S WALK interval (5 s), then flashing DON'T WALK for the rest of the green) and resets T_EWW (E/W WALK interval (3 s)).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(S:FS) Examine If Closed asks: true when S:FS is on.
  2. A branch of 9 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(2,Step) Move does: puts 2 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(NS_Ped_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches NS_Ped_Req. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 3
    1. OTU(EW_Ped_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches EW_Ped_Req. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 4
    1. RES(T_NSG) Reset does: resets T_NSG. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 5
    1. RES(T_NSX) Reset does: resets T_NSX. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 6
    1. RES(T_EWG) Reset does: resets T_EWG. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 7
    1. RES(T_EWX) Reset does: resets T_EWX. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 8
    1. RES(T_NSW) Reset does: resets T_NSW. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).
    Path 9
    1. RES(T_EWW) Reset does: resets T_EWW. It zeroes a timer or counter (accumulator and status bits), or a control (its position and status bits).

pats.t: An unlatch.
pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears NS_Ped_Req when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

rungs.head: Cycle · Rung 0
rungs.comment: STEP 0, N/S GREEN: a minimum green, and a maximum. Each timer runs only in its step and resets when the step leaves, which is what EQU in front of a TON buys

pred.q: Step is -1. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: T_NSG is reset to 0. It stops at EQU(Step,0).

rungs.words: When Step (The cycle: 0 N/S green, 1 N/S amber, 2 all red, 3 E/W green, 4 E/W amber, 5 all red) equals 0, the rung runs the timer T_NSG (N/S minimum green (8 s)) toward 8000 ms (8 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,0) Equal asks: true when Step equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. TON(T_NSG,8000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_NSG toward 8000 ms (8 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_NSG counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.
pats.think: a kitchen timer you have to keep holding down. Let go and it springs back to zero.
pats.watch: A rung that resets its own timer’s condition (a timer that cuts its own rung with its .DN) restarts every preset: that is a pulse generator, not a delay. Make sure that is what you meant.

rungs.head: Cycle · Rung 1
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle: 0 N/S green, 1 N/S amber, 2 all red, 3 E/W green, 4 E/W amber, 5 all red) equals 0, the rung runs the timer T_NSX (N/S maximum green (20 s)) toward 20000 ms (20 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,0) Equal asks: true when Step equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. TON(T_NSX,20000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_NSX toward 20000 ms (20 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_NSX counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Cycle · Rung 2
rungs.comment: END OF N/S GREEN, actuated: after the minimum, when somebody is waiting on E/W, or at the maximum. With no E/W demand the main road rests in green: that is what the loops are for

pred.q: T_NSG.DN is on, EW_Req is on, T_NSX.DN is on and Step is 0. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written.

rungs.words: When Step (The cycle: 0 N/S green, 1 N/S amber, 2 all red, 3 E/W green, 4 E/W amber, 5 all red) equals 0, T_NSG.DN (the done bit of T_NSG: N/S minimum green (8 s)) is on and either (EW_Req (Demand on the E/W road) is on) or (T_NSX.DN (the done bit of T_NSX: N/S maximum green (20 s)) is on), the rung puts 1 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,0) Equal asks: true when Step equals 0. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(T_NSG.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_NSG.DN is on.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(EW_Req) Examine If Closed asks: true when EW_Req is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(T_NSX.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_NSX.DN is on.
  4. MOV(1,Step) Move does: puts 1 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.t: A step of a sequence.
pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 0, to 1); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.
pats.think: a recipe card with numbered steps and one finger on it. Each rung only reads the line under the finger; when its line is done it moves the finger to the next number.
pats.watch: A rung further down that tests for the new step number sees it in this same scan. Rung order decides whether the next step starts now or next scan.

rungs.head: Cycle · Rung 3
rungs.comment: STEP 1, N/S AMBER: three seconds, never shortened
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle: 0 N/S green, 1 N/S amber, 2 all red, 3 E/W green, 4 E/W amber, 5 all red) equals 1, the rung runs the timer T_NSY (N/S amber (3 s)) toward 3000 ms (3 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,1) Equal asks: true when Step equals 1. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. TON(T_NSY,3000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_NSY toward 3000 ms (3 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_NSY counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Cycle · Rung 4
rungs.comment: Amber done: all red. The N/S pedestrian request is served by now

pred.q: T_NSY.DN is off and Step is 1. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Step is not written (it keeps its value) and NS_Ped_Req is left as it was. It stops at XIC(T_NSY.DN).

rungs.words: When Step (The cycle: 0 N/S green, 1 N/S amber, 2 all red, 3 E/W green, 4 E/W amber, 5 all red) equals 1 and T_NSY.DN (the done bit of T_NSY: N/S amber (3 s)) is on, the rung puts 2 into Step and unlatches NS_Ped_Req (A pedestrian wants to cross along N/S (latched by the button, cleared when served)).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,1) Equal asks: true when Step equals 1. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(T_NSY.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_NSY.DN is on.
  3. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. MOV(2,Step) Move does: puts 2 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(NS_Ped_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches NS_Ped_Req. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.t: A step of a sequence.
pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 1, to 2); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Cycle · Rung 5
rungs.comment: STEP 2, ALL RED: the clearance interval. Two seconds: a car that took the amber at speed needs 1.7 s to clear the box, and the first car the other way is rolling 0.5 s after its green
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle: 0 N/S green, 1 N/S amber, 2 all red, 3 E/W green, 4 E/W amber, 5 all red) equals 2, the rung runs the timer T_AR1 (All-red clearance after N/S (2 s)) toward 2000 ms (2 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,2) Equal asks: true when Step equals 2. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. TON(T_AR1,2000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_AR1 toward 2000 ms (2 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_AR1 counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Cycle · Rung 6

pred.q: T_AR1.DN is on and Step is 2. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written.

rungs.words: When Step (The cycle: 0 N/S green, 1 N/S amber, 2 all red, 3 E/W green, 4 E/W amber, 5 all red) equals 2 and T_AR1.DN (the done bit of T_AR1: All-red clearance after N/S (2 s)) is on, the rung puts 3 into Step.
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,2) Equal asks: true when Step equals 2. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. XIC(T_AR1.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_AR1.DN is on.
  3. MOV(3,Step) Move does: puts 3 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

pats.t: A step of a sequence.
pats.why: The rung only acts in one step (Step = 2, to 3); when its conditions are met it writes the next step number, and from then on the rungs for that step take over. One step number at a time means one thing happening at a time.

rungs.head: Cycle · Rung 7
rungs.comment: STEP 3, E/W GREEN: the side road's minimum and maximum
rungs.words: When Step (The cycle: 0 N/S green, 1 N/S amber, 2 all red, 3 E/W green, 4 E/W amber, 5 all red) equals 3, the rung runs the timer T_EWG (E/W minimum green (7 s)) toward 7000 ms (7 s).
rungs.ltr:
1. EQU(Step,3) Equal asks: true when Step equals 3. Both values are compared every scan.
  2. TON(T_EWG,7000,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_EWG toward 7000 ms (7 s). The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_EWG counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Cycle · Rung 8

pred.q: Step is 2. What does the rung do?

rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_Fl.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_Fl.DN is on.
  2. TON(T_Fl2,500,0) Timer On Delay does: runs the timer T_Fl2 toward 500 ms. The accumulator counts while the rung is true; .DN comes on at the preset; the moment the rung goes false the timer resets.

pats.t: A timer: it times only while this rung is true.
pats.why: T_Fl2 counts while the rung is true; its .DN comes on at the preset, and the moment the rung goes false it is back at zero. Other rungs read .DN (or .ACC) to act on the time.

rungs.head: Monitor · Rung 2

pred.q: T_Fl.DN is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Fl_Bit is off. It stops at XIC(T_Fl.DN).

rungs.words: When T_Fl.DN (the done bit of T_Fl: Flasher, half a second on) is on, the rung turns Fl_Bit (The flasher bit, 1 Hz) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(T_Fl.DN) Examine If Closed asks: true when T_Fl.DN is on.
  2. OTE(Fl_Bit) Output Energize does: turns Fl_Bit on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Monitor · Rung 3
rungs.comment: FLASH MODE: the cabinet selector, or the conflict monitor has tripped. The MMU flashes the heads itself in hardware; the program follows so the cycle restarts cleanly from all-red when it is reset
rungs.words: When either (Mode_Sel_Pos2 (Mode_Sel Pos2: 1 in the right-hand position) is on) or (MMU_Fault (Intersection MMU_Fault: Conflict monitor tripped: the cabinet is in red flash until the MMU is reset (click the cabinet)) is on), the rung turns Flash (Flash mode: the selector, or the conflict monitor has tripped) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. A branch of 2 parallel paths: power gets through if any one of them is true.
    Path 1
    1. XIC(Mode_Sel_Pos2) Examine If Closed asks: true when Mode_Sel_Pos2 is on.
    Path 2
    1. XIC(MMU_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when MMU_Fault is on.
  2. OTE(Flash) Output Energize does: turns Flash on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Monitor · Rung 4
rungs.comment: Flashing: hold the cycle at all-red, so it comes back with a clearance, never into a green

pred.q: Flash is on. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is true: Step is written.

rungs.words: When Flash (Flash mode: the selector, or the conflict monitor has tripped) is on, the rung puts 2 into Step (The cycle: 0 N/S green, 1 N/S amber, 2 all red, 3 E/W green, 4 E/W amber, 5 all red).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Flash) Examine If Closed asks: true when Flash is on.
  2. MOV(2,Step) Move does: puts 2 into Step. It writes every scan the rung is true.

rungs.head: Monitor · Rung 5
rungs.comment: Cabinet lamps
rungs.words: When Flash (Flash mode: the selector, or the conflict monitor has tripped) is off, the rung turns Lamp_Run_On (Lamp_Run On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIO(Flash) Examine If Open asks: true when Flash is off.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Run_On) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Run_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Monitor · Rung 6

pred.q: MMU_Fault is off. What does the rung do?
pred.a: The rung is false: Lamp_Fault_On is off. It stops at XIC(MMU_Fault).

rungs.words: When MMU_Fault (Intersection MMU_Fault: Conflict monitor tripped: the cabinet is in red flash until the MMU is reset (click the cabinet)) is on, the rung turns Lamp_Fault_On (Lamp_Fault On: Lamp) on (and off whenever the rung is false).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(MMU_Fault) Examine If Closed asks: true when MMU_Fault is on.
  2. OTE(Lamp_Fault_On) Output Energize does: turns Lamp_Fault_On on (and off whenever the rung is false). Every scan it writes the rung state: true on, false off.

rungs.head: Monitor · Rung 7
rungs.comment: Reset drops pending pedestrian requests (the MMU itself is reset at the cabinet)
rungs.words: When Reset_PB_Pressed (Reset_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed) is on, the rung unlatches NS_Ped_Req (A pedestrian wants to cross along N/S (latched by the button, cleared when served)) and unlatches EW_Ped_Req (A pedestrian wants to cross along E/W).
rungs.ltr:
1. XIC(Reset_PB_Pressed) Examine If Closed asks: true when Reset_PB_Pressed is on.
  2. A branch of 2 parallel paths: each path is tested on its own and does its own work.
    Path 1
    1. OTU(NS_Ped_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches NS_Ped_Req. It only ever clears the bit.
    Path 2
    1. OTU(EW_Ped_Req) Output Unlatch does: unlatches EW_Ped_Req. It only ever clears the bit.

pats.t: An unlatch.
pats.why: This rung is the other half of a latch: it clears NS_Ped_Req when its conditions are met, and does nothing otherwise.

Flash.desc: Flash mode: the selector, or the conflict monitor has tripped

Step.desc: The cycle: 0 N/S green, 1 N/S amber, 2 all red, 3 E/W green, 4 E/W amber, 5 all red

NS_Ped_Req.desc: A pedestrian wants to cross along N/S (latched by the button, cleared when served)

EW_Ped_Req.desc: A pedestrian wants to cross along E/W

T_NSW.desc: N/S WALK interval (5 s), then flashing DON'T WALK for the rest of the green

NS_Req.desc: Demand on the N/S road: a car on a loop or a pedestrian request

EW_Car.desc: Intersection EW_Car: A car on either E/W approach loop

Cycle_Count.desc: Shown on the toolbar: completed signal cycles

NS_Ped_PB.desc: Intersection NS_Ped_PB: Pedestrian button to cross the E/W road (walk along N/S), 1 while pressed

EW_Ped_PB.desc: Intersection EW_Ped_PB: Pedestrian button to cross the N/S road (walk along E/W), 1 while pressed

NS_Walk.desc: Intersection NS_Walk: WALK for the crossings along N/S (over the E/W road)

NS_DontWalk.desc: Intersection NS_DontWalk: DON'T WALK for those crossings

EW_Walk.desc: Intersection EW_Walk: WALK for the crossings along E/W (over the N/S road)

EW_DontWalk.desc: Intersection EW_DontWalk: DON'T WALK for those crossings

NS_Car.desc: Intersection NS_Car: A car on either N/S approach loop (northbound or southbound)

Mode_Sel_Pos2.desc: Mode_Sel Pos2: 1 in the right-hand position

MMU_Fault.desc: Intersection MMU_Fault: Conflict monitor tripped: the cabinet is in red flash until the MMU is reset (click the cabinet)

Reset_PB_Pressed.desc: Reset_PB Pressed: NO contact: 1 while pressed
